main_text.l: nem ulterius trahere & ex ipsius Penta-
teuchi Samaritani natura eruere quam sit
οὐδὲν ὑγιὲς in omnibus iis, quæ callide molitur & μωραίνει
adversarius Morinus. Cùmque ipsemetego in Belgio
opportunam Pentateuchi illiús[?] vitiosissimi
perlegendi nactus essem occasionem,,
protenus vidi causæ falsitatem. Unde
facilius etiam amicorum monitis in
hanc fui pertractus palæstram, quod Ju-
veni mihi, ad Gigantem ejusmodi con-
tremiscenti omnem timorem excusse-
rant evidentissima & ἀναντίρρητα
quæ cum cura inde collegi argumenta. Co-
piosior & δευτέρ[illegible, ~2 letters]ος esse potuissem,
nisi nodo huic sufficientissimum cuneum
oppofuisse jam alii me censuissent. Quod
si vero neque ista cordatis sufficiant, da-
bo operam, ut aliâs armis validioribus
utar & adversarium ad ἀπορίαν redi-
gam. Prævideo quidem, quàm versutè
& callide argumenta mea, tanquam ni-
hil contra se facientia, sit accepturus,, sed dici jam
κρησφύγετα hæc parum morari. Clamitet licet in Apologeticis & ad

page.notes: The Greek words "οὐδὲν ὑγιὲς", "δευτέρ[...]ος" and "ἀναντίρρητα" are read from a small, worn print and may be imperfect. The glyph after "δευτέρ" is unclear. The "ὑγιὲς" reading and the accent on "μωραίνει" are uncertain. "illiús" carries an unclear mark. The line-start fragment "nem" is a fragment and is kept as printed. The paragraph continues from the previous page and runs to the catchword without a break.
